Hyperthyroidism is caused by Grave's disease which is an autoimmune disease. Calsequestrin is the correct answer. It is a Ca2+ binding protein that keeps Ca2+ locked in the SR of the cell, so that the concentration is high enough for release but low enough so that it is not toxic to the cell.  Calbindin is also a Ca2+ binding protein, but it is found in the smooth ER of myocytes in visceral smooth muscle (ie. in the gut wall).  Phospholamban inhibits SERCA, but this inhibition is removed by phosphorylation.  SERCA is the Ca2+ pump that actively pumps Ca2+ into the SR.  Calmodulin is a Ca2+ binding protein that is involved in smooth muscle contraction. It binds Ca2+ and becomes activated, and then phosphorylates myosin light chain kinase (MLCK) which phosphorylates myosin light chain, allowing contraction. Vitamin A is also known as retinol and is found in carrots, leafy greens and liver. It is also known as vitamin eye as it is essential for the formation of Rhodopsin.
